title: Voy A Versus Intento
voice_notes: Warm, patient teacher. One voice. Brian v3. English prompts use language_code en; Spanish reveals use language_code es. Avoid Language Transfer branding.

segments.say: English uses to in both of these sentences. Spanish makes a difference.
Voy a means I am going to.
segments.show:
voy a =
I am going to

segments.say: Voy a.
Continue is continuar.
Say: I am going to continue.
Voy a continuar.
Intento means I am trying.
Now say: I am trying to continue.
Intento continuar.
Hear the difference? Going uses a. Trying goes straight to the verb.
Now use the same contrast with see them.
See them is verlos.
Say: I am going to see them.
segments.word: I am going to see them

segments.say: Voy a verlos.
Now say: I am trying to see them.
segments.word: I am trying to see them

segments.say: Intento verlos.
One stretch. I am going to try starts with voy a.
segments.show:
I am going to try
voy a intentar

segments.say: Say: I am going to try to see them.
segments.word: I am going to try to see them

segments.say: Voy a intentar verlos.
Good. The a came from going, not from trying.

caption: Easy reps for the difference: voy a continuar, intento continuar. Then voy a verlos, intento verlos.
